title: How Old Is Everything, Really?
lines: Start with you. | A long life is about eighty years.
The Great Pyramid of Giza is about four and a half thousand years old.
Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing | than to the building of that pyramid.
Our species appeared about three hundred thousand years ago.
The last dinosaurs died out sixty-six million years ago.
And {T.rex~Tee rex} lived closer to us | than to Stegosaurus.
Sharks are even older than trees.
The Earth itself formed four and a half billion years ago.
And the universe began about thirteen point eight billion years ago.
Now squeeze all of that onto a hundred-meter running track.
The dinosaurs vanish half a meter from the finish line. | Our species: the last two millimeters.
And all of written history? | Thinner than a human hair.
If you could visit any moment on that track, | where would you go? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: All of written history | is thinner than a human hair.
